check.explanation: Cash (MH 2049 as published) vs the NAS concept of fincorp's control r3b.union_nas_concept, which the SAM cells hold. Bridge (Union Finance Accounts 2023-24 and RBI State Finances, the inputs fincorp uses): minus interest paid inside G_CEN to reserve funds, FCI and other funds (2049.05.101/.103/.105, 60.107, 60.111); minus management of debt (01.305, a fee, not D41); minus the deduct-recoveries lines (01.911, 03.911, 05.911); minus accrued interest and premium received on re-issues (Receipt MH 0049.03.116/.117); plus the States' interest on NSSF loans (App. II ii.b), which NSSF (inside G_CEN) passes to small savers as R8a. The Centre's own interest to NSSF (2049.01.121/.122/.125) leaves MH 2049 as an intra-G_CEN item and returns as NSSF interest to savers, so the two cancel and are not listed. The rest is fincorp's band movement in balancing (re-registered for the Wave C audit fix, 2026-10-01, audit BS-14): the SAM's Union interest under r3b.union_nas_concept (target 10,86,513.97, +-3% because the NSSF interest to savers is estimated) goes 10,87,704.16 -> 11,11,221.29, inside the band (not binding). Balancing raised the Union interest received by the accounts whose priors are in deficit, insurers and PFs (E_INSP, fincorp-31) and banks (E_BANK, fincorp-2), on dated and other securities (fincorp explanations R3a); no cash source supports the rise, which is within the band's allowance for the estimated NSSF interest.
